newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products gain with futures, except fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products gain with futures, except fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were stronger on Thursday, except for steady fuel, traders said.
Naphtha prices ended $3 higher at $223/$225 cif.

Traders said cargoes were on the move as several large Skikda pieces were either going to the States or to Northwest Europe. High freight rates forced cargoes to be co-loaded, but the arb to the U.S. was not clearly attractive.
A 28,000 tonne Skikda cargo was heading to Tarragona, Spain, for early February loading, and possibly another cargo later in the month, a trader said.
Gasoline prices rose with the recent sharp gains in crude.
High sulphur fuel oil was notionally unchanged. While Italian and Syrian barrels were well supplied for February, demand was patchy. February swaps talked around $91/$92 fob Med.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady to firmer. Two cargoes were available out of Scandinavia in February and another large one may also be offered out of the U.K.
Straight-run fuel oil was seen available in the form of F-5, which was heard offered at a premium of around $9 or $10 over the mean/mean/mean of published quotes.
Another F-5 cargo, loading in Sevastopol this weekend, was heard placed earlier in the week. The price was p+c.
Gas oil was up to $7 a tonne stronger on the back of firmer IPE futures even though some premiums slipped.

Premiums for Russian gas oil cargoes came under pressure from the good level of supply. A 10,000 tonne parcel was sold at high cif quotes -$1 cif Genoa compared with talk on Wednesday of -50 cents. "There's a few cargoes around with sellers offering at quotes high cif flat," said one trader.
FOD premiums were broadly steady pegged around Feb IPE +$2-2.50, even though mild weather was limiting demand.
